Working tree diff vs HEAD is 100% CRLF line-ending noise (snapshot artifact), no semantic changes
evidence: git diff .editorconfig, src/flask/globals.py — every line only gains \r

revise.statement: 3.2.0 merges AppContext and RequestContext (#5812); RequestContext is deprecated alias; combined context pushed per request/CLI command
Session is now lazily loaded on first access in the merged context (3.2 change)
12 Flask dispatch methods now take ctx: AppContext as first param; __init_subclass__ detects old-signature overrides, warns, monkey-patches subclass (remove_ctx) and base (add_ctx)

Shim annotation-detection heuristics are fragile: annotations not matching name 'ctx' or ending 'AppContext' (e.g. 'AppContext | None', t.Any) trigger false-positive warning and wrapping that breaks new-signature subclasses
The shim's warning/wrapping path has no direct test coverage in this snapshot
evidence: grep of Flask subclasses in tests

revise.statement: Behavior change: request inside an existing app context now pushes a NEW combined context; g is not shared; teardown_appcontext runs once per context pop (twice in nested case)
Snapshot predates Flask 3.1.3 security release (GHSA-68rp-wp8r-4726 / CVE-2026-27205: Vary: Cookie not added when session accessed in some ways); vulnerable code present
evidence: grafana commit 'update dependency flask to v3.1.3 [security]'

revise.statement: Locked werkzeug 3.1.3 (uv.lock) is affected by multiple CVEs: CVE-2025-66221 (Windows device names, fixed 3.1.6), CVE-2025-61911/61912, CVE-2026-21860, CVE-2026-27199 (affects even 3.1.5)
Docs lag code for 3.2: appcontext.rst still describes legacy model, 'requet' typo (line 122), no versionchanged:: 3.2 markers in narrative docs
View.decorators is a shared mutable ClassVar list — in-place mutation leaks across subclasses
MethodView.dispatch_request asserts instead of returning 405 for unimplemented methods
CI is strong: SHA-pinned actions, uv --locked, matrix 3.10-3.14 incl. free-threading and PyPy, tests-min/tests-dev, OIDC PyPI publish, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH

hypotheses.statement: This snapshot is a healthy, well-maintained framework repo mid-way through its largest internal refactor (context merge); the dominant risks are (a) compat breakage from the merge + signature shim for the extension ecosystem, (b) stale security posture in the locked dev dependency versions, (c) docs lagging the refactor

revise.statement: Blueprint.register mutates app.blueprints and locks _got_registered_once BEFORE deferred functions and nested registrations run; a failing registration leaves the blueprint permanently half-registered
App.add_url_rule adds the rule to url_map before the endpoint-collision check; failed re-registration leaves an orphan rule

Sansio purity contract (no IO, no Flask globals) is violated in 4 places: default template ctx processor uses app_ctx global; sansio imports create_logger which imports request global; Blueprint.register touches cli (IO-layer-only); make_config reads env
View.decorators is a shared mutable ClassVar; MethodView.dispatch_request asserts (500, and TypeError under -O) instead of 405 for unimplemented methods
Streaming template signal asymmetry: before_render_template sent eagerly, template_rendered only on full generator exhaustion

The __init_subclass__ signature shim can break working new-signature subclasses via annotation misclassification and is globally monkey-patching; it needs tests and narrowing

revise.statement: get_debug_flag: any FLASK_DEBUG value not in {0,false,no} is truthy — 'off', 'disabled', 'FALSE' variants enable debug mode
Docs claim SESSION_COOKIE_PARTITIONED implicitly enables SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE; no code does this — Partitioned-without-Secure cookies are dropped by browsers (CHIPS)
from_prefixed_env crashes with unhandled TypeError when env has both a leaf (FLASK_A) and a parent (FLASK_A__B) key

stream_with_context pushes the context at setup (view thread); pop occurs at stream exhaustion — breaks if the response iterable is consumed in a different thread (3.1.2 design was thread-agnostic); same-thread path OK

evidence: ctx.py:432 pop(exc=None) no sys.exc_info() fallback (3.1 used sentinel)
revise.statement: Manual ctx.pop() inside an except block now passes None to teardown funcs instead of the active exception (behavior change from 3.1)
